'''Omonoimi Shrine (Tobishima, Sakata)''' is a shrine in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Dewa Province]]. It is a candidate for {{ill|Womonoimino Shrine|lt=Womonoimino Shrine|qid=Q135040052|1=Womonoimino Shrine}}.<ref>[https://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=182139 DB]</ref>

'''Omonoimi Shrine''' (小物忌神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Tobishima (Yamagata)|ja|飛島 (山形県)|qq=draft}}, an isolated island in {{ill|Sakata|ja|酒田市|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|ja|山形県|qq=draft}}, Japan. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft}} was District Shrine.<ref>In January
 1946, it was recognized as equivalent to a Prefectural Shrine Rank (''Shrine Registry''). In ''Yamagata Prefecture Shrine Gazetteer,'' it is noted that the shrine may have been listed as a Village Shrine or Prefectural Shrine during its time as Ōmiya Shrine.</ref> Another shrine with the same name exists within Sakata City.
== Deities ==
* {{ill|Shinatsuhiko|lt=Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|級長津彦命|qq=draft}}
* {{ill|Shinatsuhiko|lt=Shinatobe-no-Mikoto|ja|級長戸辺命|qq=draft}}
== History ==
The date of the shrine's founding is unknown. Shrine tradition claims it was enshrined from {{ill|Tatsuta Taisha|ja|龍田大社|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|Yamato Province|qq=draft}}. It is considered a candidate for the {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft}} listed in the ''{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō|ja|神名帳考証|qq=draft}}, Volume 5,''<ref>''Jinmyōchō Kōshō'' is included in ''Complete Works on Shinto, Volume 1.''</ref> which states that the Omonoimi Shrine now located on Tobishima enshrines a wind deity, identified in the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft}}'' as {{ill|Wakumusubi|ja|和久産巣日神|qq=draft}}.<ref>The wind deity mentioned is the same as the deity enshrined at Tatsuta Taisha. In the ''Kojiki,'' the wind deity is named Shinatsuhiko-no-Kami. In the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft}},'' this deity is written as Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto. This name is an alternate for Shinatobe-no-Mikoto, born from the breath of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊奘諾尊|qq=draft}} as he dispelled morning mist (''Shin Birth Section, Variant 6''). Wakumusubi is a deity of grains and sericulture and the parent deity of {{ill|Toyouke-bime|ja|豊受比売命|qq=draft}}.</ref>
According to the ''Yamagata Prefecture Shrine Gazetteer,'' in 1738, the shrine's name was changed to Ōmiya Shrine, prompting many other shrines to adopt the name Omonoimi Shrine without substantiation. To address this, Shirazaki Yoshimi, director of the Sakata City Kōkyū Bunko Foundation, conducted a personal investigation and concluded that Ōmiya Shrine on Tobishima was the true Omonoimi Shrine. Through his appeals, the shrine's name was officially restored to Omonoimi Shrine on July 10, 1942.
=== Timeline ===
* Said to have been enshrined from Tatsuta Taisha.
* 878 - Promoted to Lower Fifth Rank, Ninth Court Rank (applies to the Shikinai Omonoimi Shrine).
* 880 - Promoted to Upper Fifth Rank (same as above).
* 1738 - Renamed Ōmiya Shrine.
* July 10, 1942 - name restored to Omonoimi Shrine.

== Transportation ==
* From {{ill|Sakata Port|ja|酒田港|qq=draft}}, take the regular ferry ''Tobishima'' to Katsuura Port (1 trip per day, approximately 75 minutes travel time), then walk about 20 minutes.
